newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch institutions' assets surged in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Dutch institutions' assets surged in 1996.

text.p: The value of assets held by large Dutch insurers and investment funds surged by more than 100 billion guilders to 896.6 billion guilders in 1996, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said on Thursday.

The seven largest Dutch insurers and the pension funds had total share investments of 258.2 billion guilders by the end of 1996, up about 67 billion from the year-earlier-period. Shares now make up 29 percent of institutional investments.
The value of institutional bond investments went up by about 47 billion to 254.7 billion guilders.
Shares and bonds together now make up 57 percent of institutional portfolios, compared with 50 percent one year ago. At the pension funds, some 60 percent is now invested in shares.

The CBS said that of last year's 67 billion guilders rise in the value of share investments, about 50 billion was caused by a rise of underlying share prices. The 47 billion guilders rise in the bond sector was almost entirely caused by new purchases. Price changes played practically no role at all in this sector.
The bureau said Dutch life insurers had sold single-premium annuity policies worth a total of 5.3 billion guilders in 1996, an increase of 700 million guilders on 1995.
Sales of new individual life insurance policies totalled 8.5 billion guilders last year compared with 7.4 billion in 1995.
